description: Check a DMARC record before you publish it or when DMARC reports or enforcement do not behave as expected. Send the TXT record text (for example 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com') and, optionally, the domain it is published for. Get back whether receivers read it at all, the policy that applies to the domain, to existing subdomains and to non-existent subdomains (with test mode t=y applied), DKIM and SPF alignment, the form of each aggregate and failure report address (scheme, destination domain, whether it needs an external-report authorization record and that record's name), and each problem with its RFC section. Checked against RFC 9989 (May 2026, which replaced RFC 7489); the old pct, rf and ri tags are read and flagged as historic. No DNS query is made, and the mailbox part of a report address is never echoed back. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/dmarc-record-check). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

domain.description: Optional: the domain the record is for (example.com, or _dmarc.example.com). Used to tell which report addresses are outside that domain.

record.description: The DMARC TXT record text, starting with v=DMARC1 (several strings of one TXT record joined without spaces).
